families.name: Tetradymites
families.subtitle: Bi2Te3 and Bi–Sb–Te–Se alloys
families.description: Layered rhombohedral chalcogenides built from Te–Bi–Te–Bi–Te quintuple layers held together by van der Waals gaps. Bi2Te3-based alloys have been the workhorse near-room-temperature thermoelectrics for decades, and the same compounds (Bi2Se3, Bi2Te3, Sb2Te3) were among the first 3D topological insulators with a single surface Dirac cone. Strong spin–orbit coupling from Bi/Sb and Te drives both the band inversion and the favourable multi-valley band structure.

families.name: Skutterudites
families.subtitle: CoSb3 and filled cage compounds
families.description: Cubic MX3 pnictides of corner-sharing MX6 octahedra that leave two large voids per conventional cell. Filling these voids with rare-earth, alkaline-earth or alkali "rattlers" scatters heat-carrying phonons while largely preserving the electronic structure — the textbook phonon-glass / electron-crystal concept. Mid-temperature (500–850 K) power generation.

families.name: Half-Heuslers
families.subtitle: 18-electron XYZ and topological XPtBi
families.description: Three interpenetrating fcc sublattices with one vacant site. 18-valence-electron compounds (ZrNiSn, NbFeSb, ZrCoSb …) are robust, high-temperature thermoelectrics with large power factors. Heavy-element members such as YPtBi and LuPtBi have an inverted, zinc-blende-like band ordering and were proposed as a tunable family of topological insulators/semimetals.

families.name: Zintl phases
families.subtitle: Mg3Sb2, Yb14MnSb11, AZn2Sb2 and friends
families.description: Electropositive cations donate electrons to covalently bonded anionic substructures, giving valence-precise semiconductors with intrinsically complex unit cells and low lattice thermal conductivity. n-type Mg3(Sb,Bi)2 rivals Bi2Te3 near room temperature, Yb14MnSb11 operates above 1200 K, and Eu-based Zintl compounds host magnetic topological phases.

families.name: IV–VI chalcogenides
families.subtitle: PbTe, SnTe, SnSe, GeTe
families.description: Narrow-gap lead and tin chalcogenides hold most of the high-zT records through band convergence, nanostructuring and strong anharmonicity. SnTe and Pb1-xSnx(Se,Te) are topological crystalline insulators where mirror symmetry, not time reversal, protects the surface states.

families.name: Topological semimetals
families.subtitle: Bi–Sb, Cd3As2, Na3Bi, TaAs, WTe2, ZrTe5
families.description: Gapless topological phases with linearly dispersing bulk bands. They show ultrahigh mobility, giant magnetoresistance and strong Nernst/magneto-thermoelectric responses, which makes them an emerging frontier where topology and thermoelectric transport meet. Elemental Bi and Sb, the parents of the first 3D topological insulator Bi1−xSbx, are also exhibited here.

families.name: More thermoelectrics
families.subtitle: Mg2(Si,Sn), Cu2Se, BiCuSeO
families.description: Other important families: earth-abundant Mg2X antifluorites with converging conduction bands, liquid-like superionic Cu2Se, and layered oxyselenides with intrinsically low thermal conductivity.

materials.name: Bismuth telluride
materials.thermoelectric: n- and p-type, best near 300–450 K

materials.name: YPtBi
materials.topology: Band-inverted half-Heusler (topological semimetal / TI under strain)

materials.name: Tin selenide
materials.thermoelectric: p- and n-type, record zT above 750 K

materials.name: Antimony
materials.topology: Semimetal with non-trivial Z2 band topology

materials.name: Bi1−xSbx alloy
materials.topology: First experimentally observed 3D topological insulator (0.07 < x < 0.22)

materials.name: Zirconium pentatelluride
materials.topology: Near a strong/weak TI phase boundary (Dirac semimetal-like transport)
